## J01 — Technical inventory and recovery

Hypothesis: this installed Windows build is the expected Mono Unity title and its content/code are inspectable.
Experiment: full SHA-256 inventory, managed metadata scan, PE imports/architecture, UnityPy serialized-content scan, all-assembly ilspycmd export, full AssetRipper reconstruction.
Result: Unity 2021.3.33f1, Steam build 21587608/player 1.4.1; 143 assemblies, 28,648 types, 18 native PE files, 1,472 bundles, 218 banks. 143 decompilations succeed; 19,679 source files. AssetRipper exports 86 scenes and 53 DLLs by default, not full source reconstruction.
Evidence: work/inventory/, work/decompiled/, work/assetripper/53efd194cd207e66/.
Conclusion: enough recovery to run architecture experiments. No original shader source in scanned shader records. Revisit inventories on input/tool changes.

## J03 — Decompiler language mismatch and real source blockers

Hypothesis: default decompiler project output can be fed directly to Unity's compiler.
Experiment: full RoR2 decompile then compile with current Roslyn and exact editor C#9 compiler.
Result: default modern source produced 7,841 C#9 syntax errors. Re-exporting as CSharp9_0 reduces both compiler probes to the same 11 unique first-pass accessibility/ambiguity errors (CS0053×4, CS0507×4, CS0122×2, CS0104×1).
Evidence: work/recompile-progress.log preserves initial counts; work/recompile-csharp9.log and work/experiments/recompile/result.json preserve corrected results; work/inventory/decompilation-csharp14.json vs decompilation.json.
Conclusion: pin decompiler language; don't rewrite syntax by hand. Revisit remaining 11 errors only if source fallback is selected; resolving them may expose further errors.

## J506 — Fresh-editor builds lost bundle-rooted assemblies; preserve them explicitly

Hypothesis: the J505 stripping regression comes from the linker command, not from the
descriptors. Comparing the last `UnityLinker` command of the J503 build
(`work/lab-editor-20261012T051749.817522Z.log`) with J505's
(`work/lab-editor-20261017T054200.839686Z.log`) confirmed it: the `--include-link-xml`
sets match, but J503 passed 12 `--include-unity-root-assembly` entries and J505 only 4
(`Assembly-CSharp`, `UnityEngine.UI`, `Unity.TextMeshPro`, `RoR2`). The missing 8 are
`Unity.ResourceManager`, `KinematicCharacterController`, `Rewired_Core`,
`Unity.Postprocessing.Runtime`, `GenericIK`, `AK.Wwise.Unity.API`,
`AK.Wwise.Unity.API.WwiseTypes` and `com.unity.multiplayer-hlapi.Runtime`. Unity roots an
assembly when it has seen that assembly's types serialized, and asset bundles built earlier
in the same editor process count. Every earlier editor session ran `BuildAssetBundles`
(`LabBuild.cs`) before its first player build, and later code-only builds in that session
kept 12 or 13 roots. J505's restarted editor only ran code-only builds, which reuse the
payload and skip `BuildAssetBundles`, so `Unity.ResourceManager` lost J33's reflected
operation constructors. The cause was editor-process history, not a repository input.

Change: `whole_catalog.preservation_descriptor` writes the whole-catalog `link.xml` and
marks those 8 assemblies `preserve="all"`, reproducing J503's rooted set independent of
editor history. That covers J33's four types (``ProviderOperation`1``, `GroupOperation`,
``ChainOperation`2``, ``ResourceManager/CompletedOperation`1``). A host test checks the
descriptor; 157 host tests and preflight passed. No prior-art entry covers player
stripping; the mechanism is Unity's documented link.xml preservation, as in J31–J33.

Evidence: the code-only build from main `6de5e57` in the same fresh editor (still 4 linker
roots) produced APK `928b9e6031982c90d848f5ba5b444c2c3c71be9e76b24222abdc6678e43e4dea` with
a `libil2cpp.so` byte-identical to J503's (96,823,840 B, CRC `f5d57613`). Its
`global-metadata.dat` is 32 B larger. The only differences are 8 more referenced-assembly
entries and the `BeforeFieldInit` flag on three `<PrivateImplementationDetails>` types;
all other sections are byte-identical after the offset shift. Installed in place on adopted
storage, the J505 check (Commando from the ordinary menu choice, invincibility only)
reached 35.2 s of live Lakes play with 4 kills. The report had an empty error and
firstFailure, the profile still held 13 applied runs, and the captured Unity log contained
no exceptions (`work/experiments/whole-catalog/gameplay/baseline-text-patch-removal-20261017T063145.504062Z`).

Branch: `cleanup/remove-text-patches` was rebased onto `6de5e57` (one test-file conflict,
both classes kept; 160 host tests pass). The editor bridge refuses a second checkout's
project path, so its `whole_catalog.py` (the only runtime-pipeline file it changes) was run
against this checkout. APK `cf26485e5b8e5bc270b7f3dd1b0a0e9e07e3229d7202bfeb05edb09bfde53d05`
has the same `libil2cpp.so` and `global-metadata.dat` as the main build. It passed the same
check with 35.2 s of Lakes play, 5 kills, empty error and firstFailure, 13 applied runs and
no log exceptions (`baseline-text-patch-removal-20261017T064122.877682Z`). That APK is
installed now; app stopped, OLED asleep.

Revisit: if Unity changes its rooting rule or a new third-party assembly enters the
build, compare a fresh-editor linker command against a full build's and extend
`BUNDLE_ROOT_ASSEMBLIES` from that measurement. A full build still roots these
assemblies through its own bundle build.

## J548 — Policy: minimal game identifiers in public recipes

User decision, 2026-10-17: public recipes may contain the minimum game-derived identifiers and
relationships needed to locate, transform and reconstruct content from a user's legitimate
installation (ordinary asset paths, GUIDs, catalog names), provided they do not reproduce
protected content or circumvent access controls. A recipe should enable local reconstruction,
not substitute for owning the game. Recorded in `recipe/README.md` and AGENTS.md; this unblocks
the runtime-config and content recipes and migration-removal commits 3–9.

status) and a check that the local files still match it.

## J583 — Causes of the four J582 R9 gaps; script audit equal

Phase 2, from-scratch rebuild (diagnosed by Claude; no build, install or source change). Hypothesis:
each R9 gap J582 left open has a cause that the receipt, both editor logs, the two APKs and the
working editor can name without another R9 run. All four items now have one; two still need a
decision before any fix. Working-editor probes ran through the pinned MCP bridge (port 8080) with
`editor.py`'s project and version guards; bodies and outputs are in `work/receipts/J583-evidence/`.

(1) `Unity.Timeline.dll` linker root. Unity roots an assembly whose types it serialized earlier in
the same editor process (J506). R9 builds every bundle from a fresh Library, and 55 bundle manifests
reference the Timeline DLL, so it becomes the 13th root. The reference APK `5f0520d2…` is a
57-second code-only build that rebuilt no bundle. The working project's own full builds root it
too: the editor log `lab-editor-20261012T051749.817522Z.log` shows 36 thirteen-root and 183
twelve-root linker commands, and the full builds `0d9d054e…` (J542, 1,417 s) and `6d3e1526…` (J551)
have a `global-metadata.dat` byte-identical to R9's. Their `libil2cpp.so` matches R9's size
(97,061,512 B) and differs in only 24 bytes: the 20-byte GNU build-id and the 4-byte debuglink CRC.
The Burst library embeds the absolute project path 32 times; with the path replaced, its length
matches. `UnityLinkerToEditorData.json` is identical in both projects. So R9 matches a working full
build. `whole_catalog.BUNDLE_ROOT_ASSEMBLIES` pins 8 assemblies `preserve="all"`, and Timeline only
by type. Pinning it too would make code-only and full builds agree (the J506 mechanism), at
+109 KB in the baseline APK. That change needs a decision and a new device-verified baseline.

(2) `Hidden/Compositing` (`unity_builtin_extra` path ID 17000, the `TextureMixerPlayable` shader).
The build appends it after the four video shaders, as the 35th entry of `GraphicsSettings`'
always-included list. Every build of the working project that compiled built-in shaders includes
it: fresh-editor and warm builds, batch and GUI (`lab-editor-*.log`, `adoption-editor.log`, J505's
code-only builds, all cached APKs). Both R9 runs omit it (J576 `work/receipts/J576-editor.log` and
J582). Ruled out as causes, because they are identical in both projects: the file list (91,841
files), `Packages`, `ProjectSettings`, the linker report, `BuildPlayerData` type databases (paths
aside), and the object types in all 549 player data files. No project asset names the shader. So
the trigger is Library or import state that the working project has and a fresh import lacks. Open
question; next experiment: list the built-in resources Unity would include from a code-only build
in a destination editor and in the working editor.

(3) The three reimport errors. In the working editor, reading `TMP_Settings.defaultStyleSheet`
logs exactly the destination's pair: "RuntimeData is null…" and the TMP `NullReferenceException`
(the game's TMP loads its settings through Addressables, which has no runtime data in an editor).
`TMP_Text.SetText` with unchanged text returns without that lookup; with different text, even
empty, it throws (tested on a preview-scene clone). The working `TrialPortalEntry` prefabs store
the text their `tsfTrialTimer` formatter produces, so `TimerText.OnValidate` never reaches TMP.
In R9, pass 1 imported both TrialPortal prefabs while TimerText's TMP target was unresolved
(`editor-repair.log`: "TimerText does not specify a target label"). Pass 2's single batch did not
follow LabBuild's dependency order: Unity imported 9,031 `.asset` files before 4,950 prefabs. So
`iscTrialPortalEntry.asset` and `iscTrialPortalEntryDanger.asset` loaded their prefabs from pass 1's
artifacts, and `OnValidate` set text different from the stored label text. The exact text it set
was not observed. J580's control reimported `Hud.prefab`, which no spawn card loads before its own
reimport, so it could not show this. A fix with no allowance: import the dependents in dependency
layers, one `StartAssetEditing` batch per layer. A host estimate from text references gives 39
layers; the TrialPortal prefabs are in layer 1, before their spawn cards in layer 2. Not
implemented: it changes `LabBuild.cs` and needs the exact-editor and device proof plus an R9 rerun.

(4) The 251 missing-script references. The shared audit body (`script_audit.py`'s file-based
payload) hit the bridge's fixed 30-second limit, and 20 roots alone took 26 s, so splitting by root
does not scale. The unchanged body ran in an `EditorApplication.delayCall` lambda that wrote its
report to a file (`work/receipts/J583-working-script-audit.json`). `script_audit.py --compare`
reports equal. Both projects have 251 per asset in 9 of 5,132 assets (226 in `mire.unity`, 17 in
`soul_perftest.unity`), and no resolved MonoScript is lost.

The gate also counts four unity-generated file differences, so fixing (3) alone cannot make R9
`equal`. `Assets/Lab.unity` is re-saved with new object IDs on every build. The two render textures
differ only by field order. The `BlueNoise_R8_1.png.meta` difference is not a reordering, as J576

## J592 — R9's four Unity-generated file gaps: two exact classifications, one open drift

Phase 2, from-scratch rebuild (diagnosed and implemented by Claude; host only, no build, install or
editor). Hypothesis: the four `unity_generated` paths that J576, J582 and J586's R9 receipts list as
different are Unity-side serialization artefacts rather than reconstruction errors. Evidence is from

`Assets/Lab.unity`. `LabBuild.Build` creates it with `NewScene` and saves it on every build, and
Unity mints random local file IDs for new scene objects: the working file no longer matches its own
provenance-map hash. Renaming each local ID to a structural name (the GameObject's name, or the
component's class and owner) makes both destinations' scenes and the working scene identical: the
same 16 objects, every field and every reference. J586's `level0` is byte-identical to the
baseline APK's. R9 now records such a file as `local_ids_renumbered`, only for this scene and only
when one consistent renaming maps every object; a changed field, a swapped reference or an
ambiguous name stays `different`.

`crtexRush_Lava.renderTexture`, `crtexFungalCaustics.renderTexture`. The destination holds the
accepted export bytes; the working files are those bytes with the top-level `serializedVersion`
line moved after the texture fields, the reserialization signature the provenance map already
records (J553). R9 rewrote the other 12 custom render textures at its final asset save (all mtimes
22:11:33 in J586); the working project rewrote these two on Oct 13 and Oct 14 in editor sessions,
not in a build. All 14 are in the payload, whose bundles serialize the loaded objects, not the
YAML. R9 now records `serialized_version_moved` only when the destination equals the recorded export
source exactly and the working file is that file with this one line elsewhere.

`BlueNoise_R8_1.png.meta` stays `different`: it is a real content difference. The working meta
marks the texture as a normal map with mipmaps (texture type, sRGB, compression and platform rows
differ), while the destination keeps the export meta. Three Standard-shader materials of the DLC4
`sanctum` blockout use it as `_BumpMap`. The working meta was written at 05:36 UTC on 2026-10-12, in
the GUI lab MCP editor session `lab-editor-20261012T051749.817522Z.log`, between the texture's two
imports there (artifact `f0c30f3d…` then `6590c20b…`). No repo code sets this importer, the export
did not change, and R9's fresh import produces `f0c30f3d…`, the working project's first artifact.
The payload differs too: R9's bundle size report lists the texture at 32.2 KB and the working build
at 42.9 KB. So this is working-project drift from one interactive editor session, and the rebuild
holds the faithful export form. Open: the exact editor action is not in the log. Proposed
resolution: commit 9 makes the working project the rebuild's output, which restores the export
meta; that needs the usual device checks.

`Hidden/Compositing` (J583 item 2) is not a fresh-Library effect in general: the first lab editor

## J600 — Draft server-active retirement of the owned native teleporter

Hypothesis: completed-session cleanup can retain native CombatSquad callbacks
because the current owner schedules NetworkServer.Destroy and the outer session
shuts the server down before Unity's deferred OnDestroy. The accepted native
CombatSquad subscribes to the global death/summon events in Awake only while the
server is active, and unsubscribes inside the same server gate in OnDestroy.
Stage transport already yields twice under active authority after destruction;
final session cleanup has no equivalent yield. This is a specific retention
candidate, not proof of the broader managed-memory root.

Prior-art-first: community-prior-art.md's lifecycle guidance and J462's owned
callback removal informed the boundary; no blanket delegate snapshot restore is
allowed. Accepted RoR2 CombatSquad, BossGroup and HLAPI NetworkServer source is
the authority for this ordering. J594 already uses the same public UnSpawn then
synchronous destruction pattern for its exact scene encounter. Unity's pinned
2021.3 lifecycle documentation explains why this fixture requires Play Mode:
[ExecuteInEditMode](https://docs.unity3d.com/2021.3/Documentation/ScriptReference/ExecuteInEditMode.html),
[OnDestroy](https://docs.unity3d.com/2021.3/Documentation/ScriptReference/MonoBehaviour.OnDestroy.html).
No original lifecycle method is invoked privately or reimplemented.

TeleporterWorldSession now captures its exact host/NetworkIdentity and marks
possible activation before removing the inactive staging parent. Disposal checks
ownership and captured server registration, calls public UnSpawn, verifies the
network map entry is gone, then destroys that exact host synchronously while
NetworkServer.active. A never-activated, inactive, unspawned host with zero owned
listeners has a separate cleanup path whether the server is active or inactive.
Activated objects cannot take that path. Foreign/reassigned hosts refuse cleanup.
The existing stage-handoff path remains unchanged.

A read-only helper counts only callbacks whose managed target is one of this
host's exact CombatSquad wrappers, including destroyed Unity wrappers; actual
managed nulls are excluded. It never changes either event list. Before/after
counts and active/synchronous/pre-Awake context remain in ObjectiveReport after
owner references clear. Both accepted regular and lunar teleporter prefabs have
one CombatSquad on an originally inactive owner, supporting the source contract;
live activation and removal still require runtime evidence.

TeleporterLifetimeHost is staged by the existing source producer. In Play Mode
with no existing client/server, it opens a temporary loopback server, observes
zero callbacks before activation, original Awake registration, public Spawn and
UnSpawn, then original OnDestroy removal and server shutdown. Cleanup attempts
shutdown even after a cleanup failure and preserves the primary failure. It does
not load the teleporter prefab or test the actual session owner; device checks
must exercise those paths. The initial idle-editor draft was corrected during
review because ordinary MonoBehaviour Awake does not run there. Source-scanning
assertions were removed; they did not exercise the behavioral contract.

Compiler-only evidence: all 94 authored runtime sources and the final fixture
compile with zero errors against the exact editor references, without opening
Unity, running Play Mode, building an APK or touching a device. Frozen result,
response files, logs and source hashes:
work/experiments/teleporter-lifetime/host-20261019T070536.844848Z/.
Read-only review: work/coordination/codex-teleporter-review.md. The build-entry
staging tests pass (12); the shared host suite and Ruff pass. This is a draft,
not executed native-listener or managed-memory acceptance.

Claude's renewed coordination lock remains held. The installed/accepted APK is
still J585, app stopped and Nova OLED asleep; the separately frozen J599

is not staged into that candidate. Next: run the fixture through a bounded empty

## J598 — Hidden/Compositing: a second destination build still omits it

Phase 2, from-scratch rebuild (run by Claude; lab MCP editor stopped through the bridge for the
build and restarted afterwards; no install). Follow-up to J583 item 2 and J592. Hypothesis: the
shader is missing from R9's `unity_builtin_extra` because R9 makes one build from a fresh
Library, and a later build in the same Library would include it, as every working-project build
does.

Method. An APFS clone of the J586 destination (warm Library from R9's full build) ran one
code-only `LabBuild.Build` in batch mode, under the host build lock, with R9's run inputs
(`reusePayload`, Vulkan). 5 minutes, success, zero errors. Evidence:
`work/receipts/phase2-compositing/editor.log` and `result.json`; the clone was then deleted.

Result: refuted. The log compiles no `Hidden/Compositing`, and the APK's `unity_builtin_extra`
is byte-identical to J586's (535,668 B). Also compared with the working project's Library, and
found equal (so not the cause): `EditorUserBuildSettings`, `BuildSettings`, `MonoManager`,
`ScriptMapper` (the same 1,847 shader names; none is `Hidden/Compositing`), both
`UnityLinkerToEditorData.json` module reports, the package cache, `ProjectSettings`,
`Packages` and `ScriptsOnlyCache` scene classes; `ShaderCache.db` holds only two
shader-error rows. R9's own script cache lists more used scripts than the working one, so used
scripts do not explain it either. No project shader declares that name. The first lab editor
build on 2026-09-13, in a near-empty smoke project, already included the shader. So something
the working and smoke projects share, and the rebuilt destination lacks, makes Unity add it;
the remaining differences are the asset databases (`ArtifactDB`, `SourceAssetDB`) and the
3,227 folder GUIDs Unity minted afresh (J575).

Open question. Next discriminating experiment: open an APFS clone of the working project with
its Library removed, and build it once. With the shader, the trigger is in project files (folder
GUIDs are the only systematic difference); without it, it is Library import state. The device
impact is nil so far: R9's APK passed both checks without it (J582, J586).

## J607 — Retire overlays by exact identity and resume native validation at cleanup

Hypothesis: J605's overlay cleanup failure combines stale native indices with
invalid entries left after the gameplay update loop stops. The owner must
retire its own exact instances and allow native destroyed-host validation to
run before requiring an empty registry and releasing material assets.

Prior-art review: pinned Starstorm2 a9a4badd BloodTesterAnimator and
AffixSuperFire use TemporaryOverlayManager.AddOverlay with a concrete model
host and distinguish model assignment from registry lifetime. They supply API
and ownership context, not an Android cleanup solution. Current e544
TemporaryOverlayManager/TemporaryOverlayInstance and J391's earlier completed
sessions are authoritative for this version and regression boundary.

Current source reveals a specific indexing trap: removing the last active
entry while others remain can leave the removed wrapper's managerIndex
positive. Later AddOverlay can reuse that slot for a distinct instance. The
old cleanup trusted each remembered wrapper's index, so an expired player
overlay could remove a later unrelated entry. Also, the world loop has stopped
by final material cleanup; destroyed enemy/source hosts can leave invalid
entries until the original manager receives an update.

TeleportOverlayRegistryOwnership now reads only the native active registry
prefix, finds the exact managed instance and invokes public RemoveOverlay on
that verified match. It normalizes only its own proven-absent wrapper's stale
index. It never writes the registry, clears global state, restores a snapshot
or copies the manager implementation. TeleportMaterialSession verifies its
tracked wrappers are absent, yields for destruction, invokes public native
OverlayUpdate once, and still requires the global registry to be empty before
material release. Live foreign overlays are preserved and cause a truthful
refusal; the assertion is not bypassed.

The exact-editor Play Mode fixture passes native last-slot stale-index
reproduction, index reuse by a different live overlay, preservation of that
replacement during stale-owner cleanup, destroyed/unobserved host pruning by
the public update, preservation of two live foreign fixture overlays, and exact
fixture removal back to zero. Evidence/source hashes:
work/experiments/teleport-overlay-lifetime/editor-20261019T080433.919719Z/.
There were no primary or scene-restoration errors. The fixture required the
native initialized empty registry and no network session; no private Init or
global reset was invoked. Final sources compiled in the pinned editor; full
host suite/Ruff results remain J606's 883 tests with one optional skip.

## J738 — Whole-catalog builds stage only committed sources and record the commit

Phase 2, from-scratch rebuild (operator decision on J729; implemented by Claude; host only).
J729 found that the working project held staged runtime drafts that matched no commit, so no
rebuild from public source could reproduce it. Change: `build.build_source_identity` refuses
any uncommitted or untracked change under `tools/unity`, `tools/catalog` and
`android/Assets/Editor` (`git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all`), and otherwise returns
the `HEAD` commit. `whole_catalog.build_integration` checks it under the host build lock before
any staging, for full, code-only and destination (R9) builds. It checks again after the build
and refuses if the commit or tree changed meanwhile. The commit is recorded as `source` in the
build-cache receipt (`result.json`), the attempt's `build.json` and R9's result. Changes
elsewhere (docs, receipts) do not block. AGENTS.md states the rule, so both agents see it: commit
before building, a WIP commit if necessary. Four new host tests run in a temporary Git
repository; 1,024 host tests pass. Not yet exercised by a real build: the next code build after
this commit is the first. Revisit: refresh the provenance map at the first accepted commit built
under this gate, then replay R1–R8 and decide R9 with the operator (J729).

## J766 — Hidden/Compositing: R9 builds before Unity's startup callback records it

Phase 2, from-scratch rebuild (diagnosed by Claude; host only: no editor stop, build, install or
working-project change). Follow-up to J583 item 2 and J598. Hypothesis: the shader's inclusion is
decided by editor process state, not by project or Library content, and a read-only look at the
exact editor binary (Unity 2021.3.45f2 ARM64, `nm`/`llvm-objdump`) can name the condition.

Evidence. `GraphicsSettings::AddHiddenInternalShaders` appends the video shaders
(`video_YUV420_convert::GetShadersForCurrentBuildPlatform`), then appends
`TextureMixerPlayable::GetShader()` only if that pointer resolves. `GetShader` returns a static
that only `TextureMixerPlayable::Initialize` writes, from `ShaderNameRegistry::FindShader("Hidden/Compositing")`.
`Initialize` is called by the playable's constructor (managed `TextureMixerPlayable.Create`, which
nothing in the editor, packages or project calls) and is registered by the Director module's static
initializer on `GlobalCallbacks::editorAfterEverythingLoaded`. The batch startup order is
`InitializeProject → FinishLoadingProject → AfterEverythingLoaded → tick loop`, and
`-executeMethod` runs inside `FinishLoadingProject` (`ParseARGVCommands`); with `-quit` the
process exits there. R9's pass 2 (`LabBuild.BuildDestination`) and J598's warm-clone build
(`LabBuild.Build`) were both direct `-executeMethod … -quit` calls, so they built before the
callback ran. Every working-project build is queued (`QueueBuild` → `DispatchBuild` on
`EditorApplication.update`) in the resident editor, after the callback, and includes it. In both
editor logs the always-included shader lists match except this one entry, right after
`Hidden/VideoDecodeAndroid`. Correction to J598: both `Library/ScriptMapper` files do map
`Hidden/Compositing` (built-in extra, path ID 17000); the two maps are semantically equal (only
external file indices are ordered differently).

Candidate fix (not on main, not run): `LabBuild.QueueDestinationBuild` queues the unchanged
`BuildDestination` onto the editor loop once scripts and imports are settled, and R9 runs pass 2
without `-quit` (`BuildDestination` exits itself; the runner's 4 h timeout still bounds it).
Host tests pin the queued entry and the pass-2 command line; all 1,066 host tests pass. Local
branch `claude/r9-compositing-fix` (`c6e4e58`, on `38687e9`); the R9 variant on the kept
destination's commit `9e7fc0d` was `c5a5642` and is discarded with the throwaway checkout.
Device impact remains nil: the game does not use `TextureMixerPlayable`, and R9's APKs without
the shader passed both checks (J582, J586, J751).

Phase 2 is paused by operator decision before any R9 run; the kept destination is deleted.
Revisit (release prerequisite): land the fix, prove it with a working-project build and both
`./dev check-baseline` modes, then a fresh R1–R8 replay and R9 whose APK `unity_builtin_extra`
should equal the baseline's.

## J773 — Root walk names the completed-session retention; director cleanup fix releases it

Hypothesis: J769's retained `PortSession`/`SessionReport` pairs have one
authored reference path outside the existing 15-owner delegate scan. Prior art:
J391/J417 and the R2Wiki memory-optimization notes cited in
community-prior-art.md; neither covers this event.

Change 1 (0475ba8): `CompletedSessionRootWalk` in `SessionResourceBoundary`, a
Unity-free bounded read-only breadth-first walk over static fields of all loaded
types plus live MonoBehaviour/ScriptableObject roots. It is opt-in through the
launch selector and has a host test compiling the production block. Run on Thor
with Codex's 97462c9 build `0dd3f57328883d9dd927362775277b876cbf59ddaa17e0a9d0e719a15094684d`:
the walk visits 403,217 objects from 4,468 roots in 1.3 s, untruncated, with 35
read failures (post-processing ConVar type initializers). It names one path:

`GlobalEventManager.onCharacterDepossessed` → `BaseAI.HandleCharacterDepossessed`
target → `BaseAI.enemySearch.viewer` (a dead enemy `CharacterBody`) →
`characterMotor.onMotorStart` → `DirectorActorBoundary.RecordDirectorActor`
closure → completed `PortSession` → `.r` (`SessionReport`).

Original `BaseAI.Awake` subscribes to that static event and never unsubscribes
(accepted decompiled source), so every AI and the body it last viewed stay
reachable for the process lifetime. That is shipped behaviour and is left
unchanged. The authored defect: `CleanupDirectorActors` removed the
`onMotorStart` closure only while the body was still alive.

Session 2 of that run then stopped: `Unowned achievement-registration callback`
in `AndroidProgressionBoundary.Prepare`. The walk read an uninitialized static
field, which ran an original static constructor that registered an achievement
callback; the progression owner correctly refused it. The walk is therefore a
final-menu-only diagnostic.

Change 2 (763be73): `DirectorActor` keeps the exact subscribed `CharacterMotor`
and cleanup always removes the closure, even after the body is destroyed. The
walk runs only when `diagnosticCompletedRootWalkSession` equals the session
index of the runner's final menu.

| GameObjects after reclaim | 11 | 11 | 11 | 11 | 11 |

## J787 — Root attribution names original static registries that keep unloaded assets

Hypothesis (J782): the retained item-display-rule graphs, and the rest of the
~57 MB per session, are held by a small number of named roots.

Change (9e9b4d3): the final-menu walk attributes every reached object to the
root that first reached it (`rootWalkRootAttribution`), with a 2,000,000-object
budget. Two five-session attempts on Thor with APK
`c8501568817a93ad5ac5317e4d00df206e561bfa1084ec164aa9dd6201a72162` stopped in
sessions 2 and 4 on J667's LightningStake error, and a first three-session attempt
stopped in session 3 the same way. The next three-session attempt passed.
Managed after collection was 177, 233 and 289 MiB; the walk visited 753,891
objects in 2.0 s, untruncated. Largest roots:

| Root (original static field) | Objects first reached |
| --- | --- |
| `ItemDisplayRuleSet.instancesList` | 398,558 |
| `TeamComponent.indicatorSetupQueue` | 120,193 |
| `StatManager.damageEvents` | 49,145 |
| `StatSheet.fieldsTemplate` | 16,315 |
| `StatDef.allStatDefs` | 15,660 |
| `PickupDropTable.instancesList` | 11,706 |

Accepted decompiled source: `ItemDisplayRuleSet` and `PickupDropTable` add
themselves to their static `instancesList` in `OnEnable` and remove themselves in
`OnDisable`. The sample's catalog generation rises once per session (1, 2, 3)
and only `labgeometry` stays loaded at the menu, so every session enables a
fresh set from the reloaded whole-catalog bundle. The unloaded previous set
stays listed. `TeamComponent` enqueues itself on team change; only its
`[SystemInitializer] Init` subscribes the queue processor, which dequeues and
skips destroyed members. The port never runs that initializer, so the queue
grows for the whole process. The same omission means the original player/NPC/
boss position indicators are never set up (a visual-parity gap, separate work).

Change (adapted Android lifecycle, `SessionResourceBoundary`): at
completed-session reclamation, with no Run or network, remove only Unity-destroyed
entries from those two lists and from the indicator queue (live entries keep
their order). These are exactly the entries the original `OnDisable` or queue
processor would remove or skip. Removed/remaining counts are recorded per
registry. Host test covers `RemoveWhere`.

Result: Thor, APK `2679a11a5aa0f5e0429e37db6151cde776667f42cd155c56d096579952628dc1`
(code-only from 0abae2e), five sessions, all passing the abandon contract with
no runtime error. Every session removes 133 `ItemDisplayRuleSet`, 126
`PickupDropTable` and 32 `TeamComponent` destroyed entries; all three registries
are then empty, and 13 depossession entries are pruned as before. Managed usage
after collection is 162, 214, 263, 311 and 363 MiB: 52,072,858 bytes per
session, against J775's 57,380,454. The retention is real but small. Menu PSS is
not monotonic (2.73, 2.47, 2.63, 3.16 and 2.78 GiB), so the reported Boehm
"used" growth does not translate one-for-one into resident memory over five
sessions.

First failure: about 50 MB per session of managed growth is not reached from
static fields of enumerable types or from live MonoBehaviour/ScriptableObject
roots. The walk does not see statics of constructed generic types (pools and
caches), native GC handles or conservative roots. Next: a longer session series
on a constrained device (internal Nova) to see whether PSS or Boehm usage
reaches a limit, before more attribution.

## J865 — Repair the first composed-audio IL2CPP bank-observer failure

2026-10-20. Hypothesis: the J860/J863 original-owner integration can build as a
full composed player after the metadata repair. Consult the audio prior-art
map, pinned R2API.Sound initialization/bank-result distinction, original accepted
AkBankManager metadata, and J845/J860/J863 before the attempt. No community or
game implementation is copied into the authored transform or public fixtures.

pass with fresh primary-device adopted storage queries. The editor is idle on

content staging succeeds with 154 banks, the unchanged instrumented native
runtime, original-owner assemblies and same-request symbol/pre-strip/Bee capture
options. Unity compiles the current 112 runtime sources and builds the content.
The 102.477117-second player attempt then fails in IL2CPP converting
`AkBankManager.LoadBankAsync(string, BankCallback)` with `Stack empty`; the
terminal reports three errors. No new APK is produced or installed, and neither
default device check is run on a failed candidate. f1550ce0 remains the installed
baseline, stopped/asleep. The mutex releases normally.

**Cause and smallest repair.** The transform inserts the argument before
Instructions[0], then inserts the observer call before the newly changed index 0.
The emitted call therefore precedes its bank-name argument. Preserve the original
entry anchor for both insertions. Exact control-flow inspection also exposes a
second attribution bug: the selected TryGetValue false edge creates a new bank
handle; it is not the existing-bank path. Place the already-loaded observer after

## J869 — Decode pinned SDK wrapper-search order on Android

2026-10-20. Hypothesis: a version-bound static reader can replace J866's manual
search-order observation with SDK-derived assembly templates and ordered
namespaces, while preserving the native-name argument and first-nonnull return
contract. Start after independently accepted PR16/main `474597a`; integrate
main's `96a178b`/J868 and the reviewed `59a83e7`/J870 before the final record.

accepted baseline and original-audio findings. Route A, IL2CPP ARM64, Android
rendering and the desktop fallback remain fixed. No editor action, game build,
package install, gameplay launch or original-installation change occurs.

**Owner and contract.** `phone_wrapper_search.py` owns current experimental
read-only support. The `phone-wrapper-search` action accepts an explicit owner
binary request, requires the existing exact SDK pin, and stages three authored
Python readers with the unchanged private binary. It consumes no captured root,
namespace table or earlier instruction dump. Its standalone isolated-Python
invocation writes a new private report. ARCHITECTURE records setup, teardown
and boundaries; LOCAL_STATE lists the generated attempt and private device
orchestration. The action/help/dispatch fixture is current and checked.

The reader bounds the named function by the SDK symbol/code extent and rejects
backedges, indirect flow, unsupported instructions and multiple normal returns.
Known register effects and graph dominance prove the original native-name
argument at each call, preserved global-address definitions, and a common
nonnull exit for every earlier search. The final fallthrough result and actual
return operand are checked before later callee-register restoration. Namespace
and fixed-assembly strings come from file-backed pointer slots; partial/runtime
loads refuse. The formatter has one supported string substitution, an explicit
indirect-result buffer and a proven original module argument in its Darwin
variadic stack slot. Inline/heap selection must refer to that same result
object, with matching tag comparisons and no intervening alias writes.

Inspect Apple's primary
[ARM64 calling convention](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/writing-arm64-code-for-apple-platforms)
for the stack-passed variadic arguments, and Arm's
[register model](https://support.arm.com/documentation/100069/0606/Overview-of-AArch64-state/Registers-in-AArch64-state)
for instruction-dependent SP/zero-register interpretation. These supply ABI/API
knowledge, not copied SDK implementation. This is generic static SDK metadata
inspection, not a CPU emulator, new game backend or RoR2-specific reconstruction.
The qualification covers file-backed metadata and normal return paths, not a
live editor domain, loader/cache population or project overrides.

reads leave denied observations unknown. No permission or network is added.

## J948 — Link SDK target-record copy and consumer operands on Android

owner SDK as Mach-O data through the existing bounded readers. It traces seven
string-copy source/destination operands, matching offsets 0 through 288 in
48-byte steps. The pair constructor passes its record destination at offset 48;
the insertion block passes that pair at a local node displacement of 8. The
consumer's string field at 200 therefore aligns with copied record field 144.
Its mode byte lies 32 bytes into that string, and its local branch selects the
inline address or the heap pointer from the same field. These are operand
relationships, not executed constructors, field-name/layout assumptions from
managed reflection or evaluated container behavior. No captured SDK instruction
listing, table or API answer supplies an input to the reader.

ordered and distinct copy offsets, pair value/memory-label arguments, the same
node-relative header write, and the exact local mode comparison/continuations.

manifest-backed definition family after original native audio readiness and

empty table; a preexisting table must match exact source references, count and

availability, allows event-name aliases, and records explicitly observed
pre/post counts and bounded zero-ID ordinals. Hashes are not bank-event presence,
posting, playback or audibility evidence. The availability field means that
the call returned and its flag was observed; a throwing callback can leave its
underlying flag true without that observation, while startup still refuses.

original Term witnesses and catalog lease retain release ownership.

activation. Native audio requires an observed, successful admission even when
no failure string exists. A failed attempt cannot be bypassed by a later
no-audio flag. The existing unrequested/unavailable-audio decoder is unchanged.

no alpha-owned menu, control, settings or delivery behavior changes.

## J1002 — Admit measured fixed-vector shader arrays and preserve existing outputs

**Source requirement and prior art.** The source camera blur family needs a
fixed vector array that the current binder deliberately refuses. Reuse the
existing native-program/resource pipeline rather than write new blur math.
Root consults the shader-recovery prior-art ledger, pinned d3dasm

pinned editor's UnityShaderVariables declarations. They distinguish native
constant registers, array extents and HLSL declaration placement; the shipped
program/parameter bytes remain authoritative. No upstream or original shader
implementation is copied into tracked source.

**Small authored change.** `shader_source.bind_hlsl` admits only fixed-size
non-builtin float4 arrays with exact integer length/type/layout metadata,
one row, no matrix, aligned nonnegative offset and a full extent within the
measured native buffer. Each referenced register must fit that buffer.
Malformed boolean/fractional metadata and unsupported shapes refuse; existing
builtin matrix arrays remain supported. Array extents are returned to the
wrapper as declaration metadata, so wrappers must place them after the name.

Independent private review rejects earlier wrapper declaration placement,
ambiguous multiple-keyword dispatch and a stale proposed patch that differed
from the tested implementation. The final reviewed binder patch is integrated
as authored source. Root's additional fractional-offset fixture exposes an
earlier indexing TypeError, so byte offsets are checked before lane arithmetic.

## J1050 — Measure exact data reuse across every PC and accepted Android bundle

2026-10-23. Read-only host assessment; no converter, game build or device action.

**Hypothesis and scope.** J1036 compares raw whole files and one Commando object
cohort; those misses do not establish that owner files cannot supply large data
ranges after bundle decompression. Measure all legitimate-input UnityFS bundles
against all frozen accepted J850 UnityFS payloads before choosing a second large
conversion implementation. This is a lower-bound reuse census, not construction
of the missing data or an optimal delta search.

**Prior art and method.** Consulted `community-prior-art.md` and the installed
pinned UnityPy `BundleFile.read_fs` and `CompressionHelper` implementations.
Their block-info-at-end, header/data alignment, compression and directory records
supply the format contract. A private bounded reader decompresses blocks into a
native content-defined chunk analyzer without loading a global object graph or
writing decompressed game data. Chunks range from 2 KiB to 64 KiB, with SHA-256
and length as their identity. The index is capped at 2 million entries. All
source bundles are indexed before target comparison; target matches never add
new dictionary entries. This prevents repeated Android content from being
counted as PC-derived reuse. Each selected compressed file must match its pinned
inventory/accepted hash before reading, and its hash and file stats are checked
again afterward. The original installation is never changed.

**First failure and controls.** The initial version-7-only reader refuses the
observed PC version 8 before the census starts. Preserve that source/failure;
the corrected reader accepts observed versions 7/8 using UnityPy's same
version-at-least-7 alignment contract. Independent pinned-parser controls match
all decompressed bytes for one selected PC and one selected Android bundle.
The chunk controls recover every byte of identical input, recover 1,038,476 of
1,048,590 bytes after a leading insertion, report zero matches for independent
random input, and separately account for all-zero chunk reuse. Source/parser/
executable hashes are retained in the receipt. These are measured comparison
controls, not game-runtime tests.

**Complete result.** All 1,721 PC bundles and all 133 accepted Android UnityFS
payloads complete in 79.1058 seconds, producing 1,854 per-file records:

| Cohort | Compressed file bytes | Decompressed stream bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Legitimate PC UnityFS bundles | 2,865,273,795 | 7,290,790,764 |
| Accepted Android UnityFS payloads | 2,241,080,891 | 5,503,897,674 |

Exact source chunks match **1,981,313,427 target bytes (35.9984%)**, of which only
3,866,624 bytes are all-zero chunks. Nonzero matches total 1,977,446,803 bytes;
128 of 133 target bundles have some matches. The largest target,
`whole-game-content`, has 3,103,913,119 decompressed bytes and 546,541,709 matched

evidence.

(404 items, 331.8 GiB logical) and `prune-20261024T064955Z.json` (107 items,
123.8 GiB logical). Free space on the data volume rose from 37 GB to 151 GB;
the logical/physical gap is APFS clone sharing. No device, editor, install or
runtime source operation occurred. `work/rebuild` (68 GB of older
lab-project receipts) and other worktrees are untouched pending owner review.

## J1070 — Produce the accepted mesh cohort from original PC bundles on Android

**Date:** 2026-10-24. **Result:** 13,231 of 13,233 accepted mesh records are
produced byte-for-byte from original PC input on the assigned owner phone.
The result is a private mesh/resource pack, not completed bundles or an APK.
Two tangent/importer cases remain excluded; the private replay packet has not
been replaced and no whole-content conversion percentage is claimed.

**Hypothesis and prior art.** J1050's whole-bundle reuse measurement does not
resolve object boundaries, streamed vertices or import transformations. A
complete mesh cohort can instead reuse original topology/vertex content,
apply authored import settings and resolve source resource streams, without
shipping accepted target bodies. Consulted `community-prior-art.md` and the
pinned UnityPy 1.25.3 `MeshHandler`, serialized-file/type-tree and compression
readers. Their API knowledge identifies external `m_StreamData`, low-nibble
channel dimensions, v22 object extents and nested alignment; no implementation
was copied. J454/J458's topology/index/vertex identity rule prevents choosing
duplicate same-name meshes. The decoder was independently authored against
the [upstream LZ4 block specification](https://github.com/lz4/lz4/blob/v1.10.0/doc/lz4_Block_format.md).
No community assumption overrides the measured original/accepted bytes.

**Complete change.** Public `mesh_produce.py` coordinates source-only production
using standard-library `unity_bundle.py` and `unity_mesh.py`. The bounded reader
selects UnityFS 7/8, 2021.3, raw/LZ4 and little-endian serialized v22. Embedded
source schemas locate fields; unchanged fields retain original bytes. The
audited `recipe/owner-meshes.json` contains 652 source bundle pins, 7,372 source
mesh selectors, source resource ranges, destination relationships/verification
hashes and authored operations. It contains no target geometry, arbitrary byte
patches, collision arrays, compressed target frames or target float literals.
Input identity remains `6af7ed94…`; every source file/body/range is verified,
files are checked again after use, every output body must match its expected
hash, and persisted object/resource extents are independently re-read.

Operations cover CPU retention/readability and usage flags, emptying accepted
collision caches, minimal asset renames/resource relocation, external vertex
inlining, channel dimension normalization and float32 normal/tangent to binary16
conversion. Twelve Root Jungle records require that conversion. Seven halfway
components in one rock, repeated in three bundles, establish the accepted
halfway-away-from-zero rule; Python's default half packing instead chooses
ties-to-even. Three other Root Jungle mesh families also match exactly. No new
geometry, physics cooker or gameplay/runtime owner is introduced.

## J1072 — Qualify timed pre-Gradle APK iteration and install transports

2026-10-24 UTC. **Hypothesis.** Authored C# iteration can retain the accepted
Development IL2CPP ARM64 pipeline and frozen external content while avoiding
bundle regeneration, Gradle packaging, debug ZIPs and duplicate artifact copies.

contracts; J763 supplies opt-in symbol packaging. The existing shared-checkout
owner from J1066/PR #54 is extended, rather than cloning a Unity project. This

API locally and used the public Unity 2021.3 BuildScriptsOnly, StrictMode and

deploys through the editor-selected device service; it cannot preserve the

activated. [ADB incremental installation](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/packages/modules/adb/+/HEAD/docs/dev/incremental-install.md)
uses blocks of a newly installed APK, rather than reusing unchanged members of

unchanged compressed records verbatim. Java/manifest/resource/input drift refuses.

v4 sidecars are generated. Immutable normal anchors bind member hashes, packaging
inputs, signer and a verified payload reference. C#-only scripts mode is explicit;

copy/hash and payload freeze/reference. Install/sync receipts separately record
storage, hashing and transfers. Ordinary builds rehash; explicit iteration may
reuse digests only while device/inode/size/mtime/ctime match. APFS clones now
cover APK/payload/symbol/project copies and camera/music atomic preimages; their
fallback remains independent copies. Debug ZIPs remain opt-in. Exact generated
APK-only stage receipts no longer invalidate external bundle reuse; audio bytes
and unknown StreamingAssets still do. Full staging retires only predecessor-owned
C# files with matching prior Git blobs/GUIDs. No build reads a timestamped run
folder or edits authored source through text replacement.

using the staged Python interpreter's default TLS context. The first request
fails with `CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED` / self-signed certificate in the chain.

the context contains zero CA certificates. Certificate verification remains
required and hostname checking remains enabled; no archive is accepted and no
downloaded code runs. This failed case is retained, not relabelled as a platform
limitation or retried with verification disabled.

supports loading CA material into a context. Android's
[Conscrypt store implementation](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/external/conscrypt/+/c006ec00f9a6c677ebaf73b64df5f5087f9623f7/platform/src/main/java/org/conscrypt/TrustedCertificateStore.java)

finds the system directory on this device, with 125 certificate files; the
updatable directory is absent.

system certificate files into its process-local default SSL context. No device
certificate store, global configuration or user certificate is modified. All
125 inputs are hash-recorded privately. Hostname checking stays true and
verification stays `CERT_REQUIRED`. This raw-file bridge does not implement or
qualify Android TrustManager policy, removed/user certificates or a production
launcher network stack.

sizes, duration and SHA-256 are bounded. An archive is promoted from its partial

## J951 — Bind SDK preload platform assignment operands on Android

**Hypothesis and scope.** J948 derives copied-field/pair/consumer alignment but

backward definitions traverse all normal CFG predecessors and backedges without
allocating a dominator set for every node. GPR and SIMD namespaces are separate;
normal calls carry ABI clobbers. Derive stack allocation anchors and aliases,
then connect every copied buffer producer: existing field storage, grow return
with that field receiver, and direct inline-field address. Neither branch
conditions nor SDK calls execute. Require bounded file-backed C strings,
scalar/vector fragment coverage, matching terminators, mode conditions and

table. No new editor/API oracle is run or staged as a generation input.

## J1078 — Isolate parallel build lanes and measure iteration bundle compression

2026-10-24 UTC. **Hypothesis and scope.** A prepared APFS clone with its own
committed checkout, Unity instance, MCP endpoint and build lock lets workers
build concurrently without staging over each other. An explicit iteration
bundle format can reduce repeated content-build work without changing normal
acceptance settings. This is host infrastructure, not a phone-side Unity
build, runtime feature or new game-readiness claim. Architecture C is
unchanged.

**Prior work.** Read J506/J584 and J1072 before extending the existing frozen
payload, timing and clone owners. This generic editor/packaging work adds no
RoR2 reconstruction, loader or middleware adapter. The exact pinned MCP
package captures its endpoint at transport start but stores setup in
machine-global EditorPrefs; the authored bootstrap serializes only setup and
restores those preferences. No vendor package is patched. Unity 2021.3
documents
[ChunkBasedCompression](https://docs.unity3d.com/2021.3/Documentation/ScriptReference/BuildAssetBundleOptions.ChunkBasedCompression.html)
and
[BuildCompression.LZ4](https://docs.unity3d.com/2021.3/Documentation/ScriptReference/BuildCompression.html)
as chunked LZ4HC: the accepted code already used this option. The R37 stack
sample is a short compressor observation, not a measurement of its full build.

**Implementation.** `build_lanes.py` owns `./dev lane` and `LAB_LANE`
dispatch. Creation snapshots prepared inputs/project/Library with APFS clones
under the canonical mutex. Later operations select the worker's committed
source in the lane's detached checkout, using a persistent lock outside the
removable tree. Editor, MCP and writable Gradle/user state are private. Device
access refuses; canonical device ownership and explicit published APK/payload
paths remain the only deployment route. Publication verifies clone hashes and
leaves canonical current-build/iteration pointers unchanged. Teardown stops
receipt-matched processes, retains receipts/logs and deletes the checkout.
Stale-lane pruning uses the same owner, preserving recent, live and busy
lanes.

`--bundle-compression uncompressed` is explicit, lane-only and iteration-only.
It retains the complete bundle map and Unity's incremental bundle builder. A
separate exact input/membership/payload ledger skips the complete bundle phase
only on a verified match. It never overwrites the accepted normal ledger or
splice anchor. Content or payload changes rebuild bundles. Normal code-only
checks still refuse an uncompressed payload. A normal full build restores LZ4
and a normal anchor. Bundle API start/end markers distinguish compression
sampling from the larger bundle phase, which also includes preparation and
manifest completion. Ordinary acceptance defaults remain unchanged.

**Lane proof.** Creation took 163.817 s, with a shared-host net allocation
increase of 385.2 MiB (APFS blocks are shared; other host work also affects
free space). The private MCP reported the exact lane project and host
preflight passed. Inherited code-only reuse correctly refused one different
audio bootstrap DLL from the canonical source cohort; no input gate was
relaxed. A normal seed established the branch's own cohort. Relocation also
required a cold Bee native DAG, so creation does not promise a warm first
native compile.

## J1079 — Complete uncompressed texture production from PC bundles on Android

2026-10-24 UTC. **Result:** all 399 accepted uncompressed Texture2D records
now reproduce exactly on host and assigned phone: 17,424,448 object bytes and
345,301,555 external pixel bytes. This closes J1076's 43 exclusions. The phone

controls. No game APK is built, installed or launched; complete bundles and

**Hypothesis, prior art and boundaries.** Read J1050/J1070/J1076 and the
community content map before extending the existing producer. The pinned
AssetRipper source at `1ac666f47d8e9dedf96afb0b914c70d7656151ea` identifies
alpha-import configuration and its StbImageWriteSharp 1.16.7 JPEG-export API.
The [original jump-flooding paper](https://www.comp.nus.edu.sg/~tants/jfa/i3d06-submitted.pdf)
provides the public coordinate-propagation technique. Bounded observations of
the exact owner's SDK identify source-coordinate/Manhattan semantics; original
pixel comparisons identify the fixed pass/tie policy. The authored implementation
uses standard-library integer arrays and original pixels. No native SDK
implementation, target-fed pixel-coordinate table, target colour/float literal
or byte patch is copied into public source or the recipe. The native SDK is an
independent host oracle, never a phone producer dependency.

**Complete transform.** All 79 selected original PC bundles remain pinned and
read-only. The profile selects 287 raw-copy outputs, 69 ordinary BC1-to-RGB
outputs, 38 RGBA dilation outputs, four BC1/JPEG outputs and one RGB/JPEG output.
Unchanged source body fields and original pixel/mip bytes remain source-owned;
name, format/size, alpha/usage and inline/resource placement are generic
serialization/import configuration. Explicit recipe path/hash is the target
configuration input. The accepted-input gate remains fixed and no different
input build is silently admitted.

RGBA dilation seeds coordinates at every originally nonzero-alpha texel. It
compares Manhattan distance at cardinal offsets 16, 8, 4, 2 and 1, keeping the
existing coordinate on a tie before checking left, right, preceding row and
following row. Only original seed RGB is copied; every source alpha byte is
preserved. All 38 previously excluded RGBA records match with this one policy,
including complex-colour images. No per-image search result or pixel mapping
is supplied to production.

JPEG processing reproduces the source export, rather than importing a retained
export JPEG. Unchanged public `stb_image_write.h` at commit
`003501f6d7a8668ce8b6d875e34dd97ad0d5d5b5` encodes quality 90 with floating-point
contraction disabled; unchanged IJG 9b decodes using fast integer IDCT and
ordinary chroma upsampling. The authored C wrapper handles bottom-up source
rows and exact stdin/stdout RGB extents. Its new-output builder verifies both
source-provider hashes, extracts named regular source/header members, adds
authored Unix configuration, bounds/reaps the compiler and retains source,
notices/logs and a complete/failed receipt. This software is based in part on
the work of the Independent JPEG Group. Full IJG README and stb terms accompany
the generated tool. No FreeImage or Unity SDK binary/source is redistributed.

The public profile contains selectors, field bounds, settings and hashes only.
No target image or private discovery file is a producer input.

Date: 2026-10-24 UTC. **Authored phone shader control and host APK input contract.**

may emit a linked graphics program through its vertex response. Reuse J1094's

private provider manifest; neither upstream implementation nor SDK-generated
program bytes are added to the repository. Original game shader recovery and
serialization remain with the content owner.

**Actual result.** The existing public client compiles an authored texture/
uniform graphics snippet twice, changing only fragment multiplication to addition.
Both requests select `stage="vertex"`; the SDK emits both executable stages in
that complete response. The host and phone payloads, all reflection records and
empty diagnostics match raw, without normalization. The two variants are each
849 B, SHA-256 values respectively
`ed0d4fee413a27a10ee20f6e6b7143e9ef4a802b4403a70c0f71d547e33b702b`
and `1cd4105ea012fde195f8c46a5c4986d9fbca30927ef044715a07df764a865869`.

execution model 0. Its fragment module is 356 B compressed and 1,080 B decoded,

fragment request can still validly succeed with empty data; callers must preserve
the entire linked vertex response and reflection rather than use that empty
response as fragment code. No compiler/protocol change or speculative stage
parser is needed in the public owner. Its API documentation now states this.

## J1123 — Guarded RGBA phone batch loses transport; admission stays open

2026-10-25. Source-only tool case against the fixed J850 content target. The
complete phone cohort is interrupted and unqualified; no game build,
installation or gameplay acceptance is claimed.

**Hypothesis and prior art.** J1107's admitted public QEMU/GNU SDK controls and
host-exact 1,333-record profile could complete together with the previously
qualified 5,006-record regression under its revised two-job thermal protocol.
The texture conversion, public decoder and codec prior art remains J1107's;
this case introduces no new reconstruction mechanism. The frozen producer is
source `9aea69926fb6673c7a64ee45453b99cb33250576`, retaining the explicit PC input,
provider pins and existing object/resource/index interface.

**Observed result and first failure.** The v8 host driver exits after
7,141.789 seconds. Its first surfaced failure is the RGBA ADB shell returning
255. Subsequent monitor, PID and thermal-log transfers fail because the device
is unavailable. No completed production case is admitted: the terminal
receipt's `cases` is empty. Production stdout/stderr retained on the host are
empty. The orchestrator separately reports emergency/FastBoot state and a
user reboot with data intact, followed by a hot zone and a cooldown lease.
Host-file mtimes precede the later incident report; they do not establish a
reconciled crash timestamp or its cause.

The last retained idle observation is 38.6 degrees C. The subsequent 13-second
authored SDK control observes at most 37.4 degrees C, a maximum 1.00138-second
sample interval, battery 28 degrees C and HAL status 0. These are pre-production
controls. The initial heavy-producer trace/result transfers fail. Later bounded
recovery obtains the trace prefix described below; the terminal monitor result
and final interval remain unavailable. Neither a thermal cause nor successful
terminal guard operation follows from the available evidence.

**Guard and terminal limits.** The sampler runs on the device while the host
waits on the producer. Its one-second loop allows intervals up to two seconds,
uses synchronous CPU/`cpuss` sensor reads and tests staleness after those reads
return. Individual sensor read errors are skipped. The older contract permits
two SDK children and pause/resume/abort at 75/60/85 degrees C. Abort continues
the owned group before termination and permits five seconds before forced
kill. These controls do not provide hard real-time protection.

Pre-run readback observes installed R55 APK SHA-256
`111b1facec5b021c87dce03be24c9b81e913160809e685dc94b23e161786917a`.
The driver requests no game install or launch. Terminal ADB failure prevents
verification of process absence, scratch cleanup, display state and the

and dense delta endpoints. Importer size tracks these array changes while
excluding reference-pose removal, as in J1119.

original index-array channels 10–13, with absent-channel identity defaults.
Already normalized original root fields are insufficient. Pairwise squared
magnitude, a quantized ARM estimate and two fused refinement steps reproduce
the native normalization; a scalar square root alone does not. No target vector
or native library is needed. Native-class records preserve every non-PPtr byte;
matching admits one physical source with equal class/native hash/script ID.
